title: Find & Replace, Go To Special
goal: Find text inside cells, replace it without wrecking other cells, jump to just the blank cells with Go To Special, and fill every blank at once.

steps.text:
This order list was typed by five different people. Look at it: **Bangalore** and **Bengaluru** are both in the City column, and the **Region** column has gaps because the export only printed it once per group.

Fixing 3,000 rows by eye would take a day. **Find**, **Replace** and **Go To Special** do it in seconds, and this lesson shows you how.

steps.prompt: You need to **find** every “Pune” in a long sheet, and later **replace** a wrong spelling everywhere. Which keys open those two boxes in Excel?
steps.explain: [[Ctrl]] + [[F]] opens **Find** and [[Ctrl]] + [[H]] opens the same box on its **Replace** tab. Both are also under **Home → Find & Select**, and on a Mac, Find is [[Cmd]] + [[F]]. We won't press them in this lesson, because your web browser also uses them (page search and history).
wrongFeedback: [[Ctrl]] + [[R]] is **Fill Right**, which you met in AutoFill. It doesn't search anything.
clues: F for Find. Replace is the other letter you usually see next to it: H.

steps.prompt:
In Excel you'd press [[Ctrl]] + [[F]], type **Pune** and click **Find All**. By default Excel lists every cell that **contains** those letters, in any capitals.

Play Find All yourself: count the cells in the City column it would list, then type that number in ==D2== and press [[Enter]].
steps.explain: Four cells: `Pune`, `Pune West`, `pune` and `Hadapsar Pune`. Tick **Match entire cell contents** in the Options and only 2 would be left; add **Match case** and only 1.

wrongFeedback.wrongValue: Find matches letters **inside** a cell, not just whole cells, and it ignores capitals. Count again.

clues: Does “Pune West” contain the letters P-u-n-e? Does “pune”?

steps.prompt:
Some people typed **Del** instead of **Delhi**. You open Replace, put “Del” in **Find what**, “Delhi” in **Replace with**, and click **Replace All**.

What will `B3`, which already says `Delhi`, show afterwards?
steps.explain: “Del” is also the start of “Delhi”, so Excel swaps that part too and you get **Delhihi**. Tick **Match entire cell contents** so that only cells that are exactly “Del” change.
wrongFeedback: Excel doesn't know which cells are “already right”. It swaps every place it finds “Del”.
Excel never warns you. It just reports how many replacements it made.
clues: Does the word “Delhi” contain the letters D-e-l?

steps.prompt:
Absent students show **N/A** in Score and you want a plain **0** there. But the Remark column also uses N/A for “no remark”, and that must stay.

Replace works **inside your selection** and nowhere else. Select just the five Score cells, ==B2== to ==B6==, then press [[Enter]].
steps.wrongFeedback: Select only the five Score cells, `B2` down to `B6`. The Remark column must stay out of it, or its N/A would change too.
clues: Leave out the heading and column C.

steps.topic: Go To Special: pick the area
steps.prompt:
Now the empty cells. Some students missed a test and the marks were left blank. **Go To Special** searches the cells you've selected, so select the marks first.

Drag from ==B2== to ==D7== (leave the names and headings out), then press [[Enter]].
steps.wrongFeedback: Drag across all the marks: from `B2` (Isha's Test 1) to `D7` (Nina's Test 3). Names and headings stay out.
clues: The Name Box shows `6R x 3C` when you have the right block.

steps.topic: Jump to blanks: F5, Alt + S, K
steps.prompt:
The marks are selected. Now tap these in turn: [[F5]] opens **Go To**, [[Alt]] + [[S]] clicks **Special**, [[K]] picks **Blanks**, then [[Enter]].

Excel selects only the five empty cells (shown in yellow) and puts the cursor in the first, `C3`.

On a Mac, press [[Control]] + [[G]], then click **Special**.
clues: F5, then Alt + S together, then K, then Enter.

steps.prompt:
The five blanks are still selected, with the cursor in `C3`. Missed tests should count as **0**.

Type **0**, then hold [[Ctrl]] and press [[Enter]]. Plain Enter would fill only `C3`; with [[Ctrl]] the 0 goes into **every** selected cell at once.
clues: Type the digit, then Ctrl + Enter.

steps.topic: Fill blanks from the cell above
steps.prompt:
This export wrote the **Region** once per group. Sort it or filter it and those rows lose their region.

The three blank cells in column A are selected, cursor in `A3`. Make each one copy the cell above: type [[=]], press [[↑]] to point at the cell above, then press [[Ctrl]] + [[Enter]].
clues: Equals, up arrow, then Ctrl + Enter. Each blank points at the cell above it.

steps.prompt:
Someone typed `90` over the formula in `D2`; the other totals are still formulas. You select `D2:D4` and want Excel to pick out only the **typed number**.

Which option in Go To Special do you choose?
steps.explain: **Constants** selects typed-in numbers and text, `D2` here. **Formulas** is the opposite, and if you tick only **Errors** under it you can jump to every `#DIV/0!` or `#N/A` in one go.
wrongFeedback: No cell in the Total column is empty.
Formulas would select `D3` and `D4`, the good ones. You want the odd one out.
clues: A typed number is a fixed value, not a formula.

steps.prompt: In the Region list, the blanks you filled are now formulas like `=A2`. Before you sort the list or email it, what's the safe move?
options: Copy the column and **Paste Special → Values** over it
steps.explain: `=A2` depends on the row above it, so after a sort it points at the wrong row. Pasting **values** turns each into plain text: [[Ctrl]] + [[Alt]] + [[V]], then [[V]], then [[Enter]], as in Copy, Paste & Paste Special.
wrongFeedback: Sort the list and `=A2` will still point at whatever is now above it, so regions get mixed up.
You'd lose the very information you just filled in.
clues: You want the names to stay, but stop depending on other cells.

steps.prompt:
Nothing arrived on some days, so the stock sheet has gaps. The stock numbers `B2:D5` are selected.

With the keyboard only, select just the empty cells and fill every one of them with **0**.
clues: Go To, Special, Blanks, OK. Then type the number and finish with Ctrl + Enter.
